title: Determiners, Articles
learning_objectives: Choose a / an correctly by SOUND
Apply all major uses of the
Repeat or not repeat the article correctly
Solve exam-style fill-ups and error corrections

sections.title: What are Determiners?
sections.source_content: Words that fix the nouns that follow them are called Determiners. They limit, specify or quantify the noun.
sections.bengali_explanation: যে শব্দগুলি পরবর্তী noun-কে নির্দিষ্ট, সীমাবদ্ধ বা পরিমাণ নির্দেশ করে, সেগুলিকে Determiner বলে।
examples: Every boy will get a prize.
Neither of the boys went there.
sections.student_tip: Determiners always come before the noun (or before adjectives + noun).

sections.title: Classes of Determiners
sections.source_content: Six main classes: (a) Articles – a, an, the (b) Interrogative – which, what, whose (c) Possessive – my, your, his, her, our, their, its (d) Demonstrative – this, that, these, those (e) Distributive – each, every, both, neither, either (f) Quantity/Number – one, two, some, many, any, few, little, several, much, all, enough, first, etc.
sections.bengali_explanation: Determiners-এর ছয় শ্রেণী: Articles, Interrogative, Possessive, Demonstrative, Distributive, Quantity/Number।

sections.title: Articles
sections.source_content: A, An and The are called Articles. They are now classed as Adjectives (Determiners).
sections.bengali_explanation: A, An, The = Article। এখন এগুলি Adjective/Determiner হিসেবে গণ্য।

sections.title: Indefinite Articles – A / An
sections.source_content: A and An are Indefinite Articles. They do not point to any particular person or thing. Used only before singular countable nouns. a book = any book; a girl = any girl.
sections.bengali_explanation: A/An = অনির্দিষ্ট। নির্দিষ্ট ব্যক্তি/বস্তু নয়। শুধু singular countable noun-এর আগে।
sections.student_tip: Never use a/an with plural or uncountable nouns (water, rice, advice).

sections.title: Definite Article – The
sections.source_content: The is the Definite Article. It points to a particular person or thing already known or defined. Used with singular/plural and countable/uncountable.
sections.bengali_explanation: The = নির্দিষ্ট। পরিচিত বা ইতিমধ্যে উল্লেখিত ব্যক্তি/বস্তু।

sections.title: Common Noun Rule
sections.source_content: Singular common noun generally needs an article. Plural does not need the unless particularised. Wrong: I have seen tiger. Right: I have seen a tiger / the tiger.
sections.bengali_explanation: Singular common noun-এ article লাগে। Plural-এ particularize না করলে the লাগে না।

sections.title: Rules for A (SOUND rule)
sections.source_content: Use A before: (1) consonant sound – a boy, a word, a B.A. (2) yu sound – a university, a European, a useful thing, a unit (3) one sound – a one-rupee note, a one-eyed person. GOLDEN RULE: Choose by SOUND, not spelling.
sections.bengali_explanation: A = consonant sound, ‘yu’ sound, ‘one’ sound-এর আগে। উচ্চারণ দেখে সিদ্ধান্ত নিন।
examples: a boy, a word, a B.A.
a university, a European, a useful thing
sections.student_tip: university, European, useful, unit, one → all take A because of consonant sound at start.
sections.note: ARTICLE CHOICE IS BASED ON SOUND, NOT SPELLING.

sections.title: Rules for An (SOUND rule)
sections.source_content: Use An before: (1) vowel sound – an eye, an ox, an umbrella (2) consonant that starts with vowel sound – an M.A., an heir, an honest boy, an hour, an F.R.C.S. Modern preference: a historical, a humble when h is clearly pronounced.
sections.bengali_explanation: An = vowel sound এবং যে consonant vowel দিয়ে উচ্চারিত হয় (hour, honest, M.A.) তার আগে।
examples: an eye, an ox, an umbrella
an M.A., an heir, an honest boy, an hour
sections.student_tip: Silent h (hour, honest, heir) → An. Pronounced h (historical) → usually A.

sections.title: Other Uses of A and An
sections.source_content: (a) Generalizing – A son should obey his father. (b) Rate – one kilo a rupee. (c) A certain – A Mr Bose came. (d) Fixed phrases – in a hurry, have a cold. (e) a few / a little = some; few / little = almost none. (f) Exclamatory – What a thing to say!
sections.bengali_explanation: সাধারণীকরণ, দর/হার, a certain, fixed phrase, a few/a little, বিস্ময়সূচক বাক্য।
sections.student_tip: a few / a little = positive. few / little without a = almost none.

sections.title: Rules for The – Complete Categories
sections.source_content: The is used in many fixed categories. Master every group.
sections.bengali_explanation: The-এর সব গুরুত্বপূর্ণ ক্যাটাগরি। পরীক্ষার জন্য প্রতিটি মনে রাখুন।

categories.name: Groups of islands
categories.note: Single island: Sri Lanka, Java → NO the

categories.name: Generalising a class
examples: The dog is a faithful animal.

categories.name: Superlatives
examples: The more you read, the more you learn.

categories.name: Adjectives as a class
examples: The rich are not always happy.

categories.name: Possessive the (body parts)
examples: I struck him on the head.
He looked me in the face.

categories.name: Comparison / unique title
examples: Kalidas is the Shakespeare of India.
Mumbai is the Manchester of India.

sections.title: Omission of Articles
sections.source_content: No article: proper/material/abstract (general); plural common; after kind of; man=mankind; school/hospital for PURPOSE; parks with proper names; meals; seasons; title+name; factitive complement (elected captain). Contrast: go to school (purpose) vs go to the school (building).
sections.bengali_explanation: Article বাদ: proper/material/abstract, plural, man=mankind, school/hospital purpose অর্থে, meal, season, title+name।
sections.student_tip: Ask: PURPOSE of the place or the BUILDING? Purpose → no article. Building → the.

sections.title: Repetition of the Article
sections.source_content: Same person/thing → article only once. Different → repeat. Same: The Secretary and Treasurer has done this. Two: The Secretary and the Treasurer have done this. One cat: a brown and white cat. Two cats: a brown and a white cat.
sections.bengali_explanation: একই ব্যক্তি/বস্তু = article একবার। আলাদা = প্রত্যেকের আগে article।
examples: The Secretary and Treasurer has done this. (one)
The Secretary and the Treasurer have done this. (two)
a brown and a white cat (two)
sections.student_tip: Look at the verb (has/have). One article usually = one person/thing.

sections.title: Must-Know Contrasts (Exam Gold)
sections.description: These pairs appear again and again in exams. Master them.
examples: a European (yu) vs an honest man (silent h)
a one-rupee note (w) vs an hour (silent h)
go to school (purpose) vs go to the school (building)
go to hospital (treatment) vs go to the hospital (visit)
a few (= some) vs few (= almost none)
a little (= some) vs little (= almost none)
The Secretary and Treasurer (one) vs The Secretary and the Treasurer (two)
He plays the violin vs He has a violin
He lives in the south vs Go south

sections.title: Before the Exam – Quick Checklist
items: Can I choose a/an by SOUND in 5 seconds?
Do I remember: rivers/ranges/seas = the; single peak/island = no the?
Do I know go to school vs go to the school?
Can I use the with superlatives and the rich / the poor?
Do I know when to repeat the article (same vs different)?
Have I practised at least 50 questions from the bank?
